item.title: 2025 - Hobbies To Learn
item.description:
Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t2JFOA023Kk

Mental

  • Reading - Provides other perspectives, makes you more interesting Physical
  • Need to do something physical that keeps you active well into your future years
  • Gym, Running, Group Sport, Martial Arts, ect
    • Gym - Even just a small, shitty space. Pullup bar, dumb-bells
    • Running - Cardio Social
  • Getting out to talk to people - find common interests
  • Find other weirdos and maintain connections Creative
  • Writing - Something to slow down, shifting to creation over consumption
  • Inspire, engage
  • Videos - Sharing things you’re interested in
  • Feel free to keep it as a private hobby
  • Try lots of things!
    • Cooking, Film making, photography, design, painting miniatures, music, ham radio
    • Look at recommended online hobbies
    • Plenty of dead-ends, but you’ll find what fits

Hobbies do not need to be allocated to just one category

item.title: Digital Garden
item.description:
Reference: https://youtu.be/en56OKg5hyc?si=W3YCDI4uDlcOk5Nd My digital garden: https://digitalgarden.joshrichards.com.au/

Digital Garden

Seen as an add-on to traditional blogging - bi-Directional Links between Obsidian and your Blog Non-linear writing, Low effort & low friction Offers a way to build your own, future-proof, decentralised platform

Three Elements

  • #seed - Very rough and early ideas. Take smart personal notes to develop
  • #tree - Work that’s cleaned up and clarified
  • #evergreen - Work that is reasonably complete (but still tended to over time)
  • #reference - A completed piece primarily meant to support or inform others Also: atoms (single concept)/molecules(linked concepts)/alloys(crafted)

Obsidian to Hugo Publishing

item.title: Effective Note-Taking to Remember More + Create New Ideas
item.description:
Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_t9R1AnB7ho

Note-taking

Understanding and remembering more Combining ideas for more creative ideas

Two steps

  • Literature notes - Things that stood out or interested you (in your own words)

    • Punchy quotes, how you felt,
    • Write in your own words
      • Forces you to think - properly process your thoughts
      • Check yourself - Do you really get it? Do you know what you feel about it? Can you explain it in your own words? Do you get the main idea?
      • Remember more of what you read - Learning is helped by friction (req. effort so it’s an active process)

  • Atomic Notes - Based on Literature Notes but independent (without source context)

item.title: Mini Essay - Mental Baggage
item.description: One of my ongoing challenges is keeping track of and managing all the different things that engage my attention. This can mean my Personal, asking Mini Essay - What are your obligations, my Work, and anything else that contacts my senses and hooks my attention. While I can track a wide range of interests and passions, the real challenge for me is task-switching: being invested in one thing, but needing to keep something else in mind at the same time, or being pulled away from my focus to handle some other issue.

item.title: Note - Mini Essays
item.description:
Original: https://youtu.be/N4YjXJVzoZY

Short piece of writing on some thing you find interesting All about retention, learning & reflection Write fast and often - over time it provides depth Mini-essays make learning more addictive by being novel Like a sketchbook for an artist

Three rules of Mini-essays

  1. Only cover one idea
  2. Keep them short (fit on monitor without scrolling)
  3. Keep them organised (Obsidian)

Elements of mini-essay

  • 100-300 words (no scrolling within Obsidian, focus on being brief)
  • Storytelling approach? Prose? Make sure this serves your goals
  • Write it as if you’re teaching it (Feynmann technique)
  • Restrict to single concept (one distinct idea) or idea (save connection/blending for larger writing)

item.title: Notes - The Garden and the Stream
item.description:
Reference: https://hapgood.us/2015/10/17/the-garden-and-the-stream-a-technopastoral/

The Garden - the web as topology, web as space.

  • Web as arrangement and rearrangement, relational
  • Multi-linear approaches - every walk through the garden is different every time
  • “Did the bridge come after these trees” in a well-designed garden is meaningless historical trivia.

The Stream - Jump in and let it flow past

  • Stream replaces topology with serialisation (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram)
  • Single, time-ordered path with our experience (and only our experience) at the centre
  • Stream is self-assertive (Garden is integrative)

“As We May Think” by Vannevar Bush - Essay was inspiration for the pioneers of hypertext

item.title: Notes - Too Many Interests
item.description:
Reference: https://youtu.be/lQFOeC3maeI?si=NVyRDJ759R7_Uhl2

Too Many Interests

You can’t follow your interests if you have no energy

  • Working all day, overstimulation,
  • Unfair to expect all to be able to come home and jump straight in
  • More about energy rather than time
    • How do you enjoy your hobby with a fresh mind and happy outlook
  • Save the heavy stuff for the morning when you’re fresh
    • Probably start to hate the hobby
    • Tired? Focus on relaxed aspects
    • Fresh? Focus on heavy
    • Split hobby elements into “Relaxing” and “Demanding”
  • Look at your energy levels and where you can give best (for me: Mornings)
  • Woodworking vs Camping - Split your hobbies into Relaxing vs Demanding
    • Woodworking you can roll straight into (Relaxing & Rejuvinating)
    • Camping requires more setup & investment (More Demanding)
  • Money
    • Must meet basic needs to fund hobbies
    • Expensive hobbies
    • Money can buy time to embrace hobbies
  • Take a break when you get home
    • Take half an hour to relax and disconnect from work
    • Get back in creative mood
    • Figure out how to have a better break
  • Carve out space for your hobbys/interests
    • Don’t be completely selfless
    • Express that it’s important to you, and an important part of who you are
  • Say no to some of your hobbies (or atleast say no to new ones)
    • The more you do, the more you dilute
    • Kill your darlings
    • Cut it down to 2-3 main hobbies - Intellectual, Physical, Social
  • Hobby Seasons
    • Focus hard on one hobby for several months, then steer away to something else
    • You’ll have muscle memory of the hobby (so you can come back)
    • You’re free to return to any hobby whenever you want
      • If you miss something after you stop, that’s important - you may stick with it your whole life
    • You can’t do everything
  • Busy with other priorities? Find ways to do a little of something you love
    • Let the big thing go, but find small ways to do it instead
    • Reduce the time
  • Quality over Quantity - focused practice
    • Have a plan, set goals, reflect after each session (+ buy quality with coaches)

Common Time Management

item.title: Time Management
item.description:
Use mini keyboard to type before work Productivity

  • Pomodoro, Meditation, speech-to-text, Eat the frog, alarm to go to bed
  • Each evening, plan ahead for the next day. Max 10 things
  • Break down tasks, If it’ll take <5 mins then do it right now,
  • Do what your future self will thank you for, Ask why you don’t want to do a thing
  • Show up every day - It doesn’t matter how I perform, just show up consistently.
  • Practice the basics: Sleep, exercise, diet.
    • Wake up early: First hours of day to myself, then go to work tired
    • Wim Hof - 2min cold shower at the start of the day
    • Set an alarm at night to go to bed
  • Have ADHD Days & Autism Nights
    • Paint WH40k? LEGO?
    • Dream Bigger: Space Jump, Breakthrough Listen, 50 marathons in 50 days, Mini Essay - Ridiculous Bucket List

Meditation
